basis: May 27, 2022 is the first verified qualifying disclosure. Big Lots reported consolidated GAAP net sales of $1,374,714,000 for fiscal Q1 2022, below the $1,544,274,400 cutoff (95% of $1,625,552,000 in fiscal Q1 2021). Both reviews cited the same actuals exhibit. Their disagreement concerns whether May 27 was earliest. The March 3 guidance supplied no explicit numeric ceiling for consolidated sales, and the January 11 ICR and March 9 BofA management remarks remain unverified. The earliest date therefore remains open.

coverage.detail: December 3, 2021, preceding earnings cycle. The release projected slightly positive comparable sales for fiscal Q4 2021 and a low-single-digit comparable-sales decline for full-year fiscal 2021.
The December call discussed an adverse Q1 FY2022 stimulus comparison and negative comparable sales. It supplied no numeric upper bound for Q1 consolidated revenue.

January 10. The trading update covered fiscal Q4 2021. The $8 billion to $10 billion sales goal was long-term. Big Lots scheduled the January 11 ICR fireside chat for 10:30 a.m. ET and advertised an issuer-site replay through January 21.
The January investor deck is accessible as Exhibit 99.2. It documents the long-term plan and supplies no Q1 FY2022 consolidated sales ceiling. The filing does not preserve the spoken discussion.

ICR confirmed that the 2022 presentations moved to its virtual platform. Its host notice links to scheduling and registration. The [historical schedule PDF](https://assets.swoogo.com/uploads/1502532-61afb67d938d9.pdf) was inaccessible. Neither the [Wall Street Webcasting event directory](https://wsw.com/webcast/icr7/) nor a [ticker-based lookup](https://wsw.com/webcast/icr7/big/) yielded accessible audio. The latter URL could not be authenticated as Big Lots’ player.

The issuer’s advertised replay location returned HTTP 404. Both the [January 11 archive request](https://web.archive.org/web/20220111/https://www.biglots.com/corporate/investors/) and the [March 9 archive request](https://web.archive.org/web/20220309/https://www.biglots.com/corporate/investors/) were inaccessible. The contents of any archived players remain unknown.

March 3. Big Lots forecast Q1 FY2022 comparable sales up approximately 10% versus Q1 2019 and translated that to a low-double-digit comparable-sales decline versus Q1 2021. The explicit $1.10–$1.20 range applied to diluted EPS.

Slide 21 adds 130 basis points of expected sales growth from net new and relocated stores. This supports a likely consolidated decline beyond 5%, but the comparable-sales forecast has no stated numeric year-over-year endpoint from which to calculate an explicit consolidated ceiling.

The CFO repeated the roughly 130-basis-point store contribution. His 12-point estimate measured Q1 comparable-sales drag from lapping stimulus. The [covering 8-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/768835/000076883522000005/big-20220301.htm) dates the call to March 3, 2022 despite the transcript cover’s 2021 typo.

The indexed issuer wire listing records Big Lots’ March 4 announcement of its March 9 BofA conference appearance. Direct retrieval returned a cache miss. The interval search located no written Q1 consolidated sales preannouncement.
The BofA conference webcast directory was inaccessible. No Big Lots-specific event-hosted recording, transcript or deck was recovered.

The prior review reached only the moderator’s introduction to the March 9 session. The direct retry returned a cache miss. A separate [transcript archive](https://stockanalysis.com/quote/otc/BIGGQ/transcripts/) lists the March 3 earnings call and a January 2021 ICR event, but neither disputed 2022 conference session.
May 13. The issuer announced the May 27 reporting date without preliminary sales figures.
Item 5.07 reports the May 24 annual-meeting votes. The filing supplies no meeting transcript. Item 2.02 separately records the May 27 earnings release and call.

May 27 actuals. The consolidated statements give net sales of 1,374,714 and 1,625,552, in thousands of dollars, for the 13 weeks ended April 30, 2022 and May 1, 2021. The release reports a 15.4% total sales decline, a 17.0% comparable-sales decline and about 160 basis points of growth from net new stores and relocations. The [June 10-Q](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/768835/000076883522000099/big-20220430.htm) confirms both amounts.

publication_date_evidence: Big Lots’ original wire release is timestamped May 27, 2022 at 6:00 a.m. ET, matching the Exhibit 99.1 dateline and the release date in Item 2.02. This establishes when the actuals became public. The missing conference remarks prevent verification of the earliest qualifying disclosure. [Issuer wire release](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/big-lots-reports-q1-results-301556383.html)
